bullets.title: PCE inflation marginally above target; Fed hold likely but rates still restrictively high
bullets.body: July PCE came in at +0.2% m/m vs. +0.1% expected and +3.7% y/y vs. +3.6% est., while core PCE held steady at +3.3% y/y matching consensus. Capital Economics sees no September hike, but 65 consecutive months above the 2% target and a 3.0-3.5% annualized core rate keep the door open to higher-for-longer. Notably, more than half of July's core PCE gain was attributed to portfolio management/investment advisory fees tied to equity-market gains rather than broad underlying price pressures.

bullets.title: Q2 GDP confirmed at +1.5%; consumer spending beats at +3.4% with savings rate rebounding
bullets.body: The second GDP print confirmed +1.5% q/q annualized growth, in line with estimates. Personal consumption came in at +3.4% vs. +3.2% expected, and personal income beat sharply at +0.4% vs. +0.2% est. Household savings rate rebounded from a 4-year low, suggesting consumer-driven growth may moderate; durable goods beat the headline at +1.1% but the ex-transport and cap-goods figures missed.

bullets.title: 5Y Treasury auction tails for 15th straight time; yields hit session highs on weak foreign demand
bullets.body: The 5-year Treasury auction cleared at 4.393% vs. 4.391% WI (0.2bp tail), marking the 15th consecutive failure to stop through. Foreign buyer takedown fell to 11.9%, the lowest since April 2025. Yields hit session highs post-auction, and JPM notes the 7-year sector has richened ~10bp above fundamentals ahead of Thursday's $44bn offering.

bullets.title: Jackson Hole and Warsh speech flagged as key macro catalyst; JPM tactically bullish but with low conviction
bullets.body: JPM US Market Intelligence is tactically bullish with lower conviction, warning of a 3-4% SPX pullback if both NVDA and Fed Chair Warsh disappoint at Jackson Hole. CTA behavior and positioning suggest risk/reward favors lower yields. Market pricing for September rate action is effectively unchanged post-PCE.

bullets.title: Market closes near flat; equal-weight/cyclicals outperform as tech broadens beyond Mag 7
bullets.body: S&P 500 closed slightly lower on Wed with breadth positive; equal-weight index edged higher on rotation toward cyclicals (Financials, Industrials, Energy). Tech sector snapped a 7-day losing streak — the longest since summer 2022. NDX futures led into close. Industrials outperformed the S&P by ~100bps; Cybersecurity and AI/DC names led within sectors.

bullets.title: AI capex buildout accelerating to debt-boom scale; hyperscaler commitments at historic levels
bullets.body: Multiple sources flag that the AI infrastructure cycle is morphing into a debt boom, with hyperscaler capex approaching historic scale. Anthropic signed a $45B, 460-megawatt compute deal with NScale (potential IPO candidate). OpenAI and Anthropic together consume ~33% of incremental global compute, expected to rise to ~50% next year. CXL adoption increasing as memory CAPEX rises.

bullets.title: Custom AI silicon race intensifies; CUDA moat questions surface from multiple angles
bullets.body: OpenAI's Jalapeño ASIC claims performance edge over Nvidia GB300 (aided by HBM4 vs HBM3E), while Meta MTIA 300 and Google TPU v10 advance. Separately, Tensordyne claims agentic AI can now auto-generate inference kernels, potentially reducing CUDA's software moat. Multiple sell-side analysts note this could weigh on NVDA's inference margins and dominance long-term.

bullets.title: AI trade broadening from semis/Mag 7 to software; Jefferies conference flags strong fundamentals
bullets.body: Jefferies semis conference takeaways show AI fundamentals remain robust — GPU rental rates, token consumption, and hyperscaler capex all strong. Recent weakness attributed to positioning/leverage dynamics, not demand. AMD secured more supply than guided with token usage up 40% m/m; AI trade is broadening from semiconductors and Mag 7 into software and cyclicals.

bullets.title: Memory supply constraints creating 'cascading bottlenecks'; pricing worsening into 2027
bullets.body: NVDA's strategic supply commitments jumped from $119B to $279B, primarily for memory procurement; extreme memory pricing expected to worsen into 2027 per Jefferies. Separately, DDR2/DDR3/DDR4 supply constraints are creating cascading bottlenecks as ODMs downgrade to older standards while legacy suppliers exit. Kioxia announced a ¥1T+ investment in a new memory plant, adding future supply overhang.

bullets.title: Iran-Hormuz situation fluid; Strait functioning but deal with Oman unfinalized; oil inventories bullish
bullets.body: Trump stated 10M barrels passed through Hormuz yesterday and the strait is functioning, while Rubio signaled no new U.S. strikes near-term. A senior Iranian source told Reuters an Oman deal is still not finalized. Kalshi market shows 50-68% odds of normalization by early 2028. EIA data showed crude inventories +95K bbl vs. +1.58M est., with gasoline -2.54M and distillates -2.29M — bullish for crude. SPR drained to 290M barrels, lowest since 1982.

bullets.title: U.S. fiscal trajectory deteriorating; debt interest now exceeds defense spending
bullets.body: Net interest payments reached $970B last year, exceeding the $917B defense budget. Druckenmiller's op-ed on entitlement means-testing gaining traction with Republican leaders. Debt ceiling X-date estimated April-July 2027; bond market dynamics increasingly important as marginal buyers reassess holdings. 30Y yield hit levels not seen since 2007 per Hedgeye.

bullets.title: S&P 500 positive gamma support; $2B+ put wall at SPY 765 kept price pinned all week
bullets.body: Positive gamma observed in SPX and aggregate single stocks on Wednesday. A $2B+ put wall at SPY 765 has kept price range-bound throughout the week. ES_F and NQ_F traded around VWAP ahead of NVDA earnings release, with NQ futures expected to trade 29,225–29,387 at 4pm.

bullets.title: US disrupts China-linked hacking operation; Fed, NASA, NIH, DoE, Senate breached
bullets.body: The FBI and DOJ seized platforms operated by Chinese state-sponsored hackers that had breached NASA, the Federal Reserve, NIH, the U.S. Senate, DoE, and DoJ. The operation targeted critical infrastructure networks. Cybersecurity implications for financial and tech sectors are direct.

bullets.title: Nuclear stocks (OKLO, SMR, NNE) declining on sector headwinds; AI/infrastructure ETF themes dominant
bullets.body: OKLO -6%, SMR -5.5%, NNE -3.8% on sector pressure. AI, Infrastructure, Defense, Space, and Nuclear identified as 2026's top 5 ETF themes. NRDC report warns Trump energy policy could eliminate 540 GW of renewable capacity over the next decade, potentially structurally shifting power mix.

bullets.title: Apple iPhone 18 event set for September 9; foldable phone and Siri AI expected
bullets.body: Apple began sending official invites for a September 9th launch event at 1PM ET. IDC projects 10M foldable iPhone sales in year 1. Event expected to feature Siri AI upgrades and potentially Apple's first foldable device. Apple also expanding ad inventory via iPhone search and 'suggested places' feature.

bullets.title: Open-source AI gaining share rapidly; 28% to 62% token share vs. OpenAI and Anthropic
bullets.body: Open-source models' share of AI token consumption rose from 28% to 62% per Gavin Baker, directly pressuring OpenAI and Anthropic. Chinese model GLM-5.3-Flash (previously 'Ox Alpha') runs entirely on Chinese chips, serves 100T tokens/day, and is beating DeepSeek on pricing in most categories. The AI model economics debate intensifying around whether infrastructure or application-layer companies ultimately capture margins.

bullets.title: Treasury 7Y auction faces rich valuations; 2Y yield range-bound near 4.20%; dollar up 0.3%
bullets.body: JPM notes the 7-year sector richened ~10bp above fundamental drivers ahead of Thursday's $44B offering; end-user share at the prior 7Y auction fell to 87% with foreign takedown at 11.9%, lowest since April 2025. The 2-year note remains range-bound with tactical support at 4.25-4.265% and medium-term resistance at 3.98-4.025%. Dollar up 0.3% on the day.

bullets.title: Strait of Hormuz risk elevated but geopolitical pressure easing; wheat at 3-year high
bullets.body: Iran-Russia advance a major gas cooperation project while Iran and Oman continue negotiating Hormuz terms. Wheat futures rose to a 3-year high on Ukraine-Russia attacks. Natural gas futures rose ~5% to $2.907/MMBtu on weather support. Saudi Arabia shifted oil exports to Persian Gulf ports to avoid Houthi Red Sea disruptions.

bullets.title: INTU cut after light FY27 tax guidance; JPM and Wolfe both downgrade
bullets.body: Intuit guided FY27 revenue at ~9% Y/Y vs. 11% consensus and cut its 3-year consumer segment CAGR target to 4-8%; Tax segment guided only +2% Y/Y. JPMorgan downgraded to neutral, Wolfe downgraded to peer perform, citing lack of near-term catalysts and skepticism around the downmarking strategy. Stock -3.8% on the day.

bullets.title: Stablecoins: JPMorgan, BofA, Wells Fargo all advancing stablecoin strategies
bullets.body: JPMorgan evaluated launching its own stablecoin amid growing nonbank competition in payments, per WSJ. Major banks including BofA and Wells Fargo are moving forward with a global stablecoin consortium. Banks are warming to stablecoins after years of executive-level resistance, driven by GENIUS Act passage and customer demand.
